correctness.rationale: An exact distance equalization on the triangle circumaxis gives the entire fourfold intersection and its p=1 disappearance. An explicit closed form for a triple witness proves the remaining nerve faces; the two omitted inclusion-exclusion terms yield the exact volume difference. The Python checker ran 8504 supplementary cases; the universal conclusions do not depend on this finite sample.

originality.rationale: The strongest directly relevant paper, Shelley--Tartakovsky arXiv:2610.25841, supplies a five-site smooth counterexample and a limiting bicone but not the four-site full nerve classification or exact escape law for product-p norms. Its construction is acknowledged, and the claim is not the general known Euclidean-ball identity. Targeted equivalent-terminology searches did not produce an encompassing prior statement; historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent four-site discontinuity may appear under older nomenclature (Minkowski circumspheres, generalized Delaunay nerves, or product norms).

The quantified four-site construction is close to the bicone limit used for a five-site counterexample in the primary source, so contribution is the complete p-dependent phase and escape, not novelty of the bicone itself.
Blömer--Kohn and some older computational geometry sources were not fully inspected; no direct positive coverage was found in the material read.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp p=1 nerve bifurcation and an exponential escape law explaining a failure of Hausdorff stability of Voronoi intersection combinatorics. It also produces a quantitative four-site counterexample at the nonsmooth endpoint to a Voronoi-nerve inclusion-exclusion reduction. A complete continuous-parameter classification supplies geometry beyond a single computational witness.
